data.name: Narsi
data.long_meaning: Narsi is the name given to the Narasimha Avatar of Lord Vishnu. Narasimha is a man-lion incarnation of Vishnu, who is depicted as having the body of a lion and the head of a human. The name Narsi represents the power and might of Lord Vishnu in protecting His devotees from evil.

in_sanskrit.name: नर्सि
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Man, human being, person. This name is derived from the Sanskrit root 'nar' meaning 'man, human being'. It is a common name in Hindu culture and is often used for both boys and girls.

data.cultural_impact: The name Narsi carries significant cultural significance in Hinduism as it represents the powerful Narasimha Avatar of Lord Vishnu. This avatar is depicted as a man-lion, with the strength and power of a lion and the intelligence and compassion of a human. The tale of Narasimha is widely known in Hindu culture and is an important part of the Mahabharata and other Hindu texts.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Narsi holds deep spiritual significance as it represents the protective and powerful presence of Lord Vishnu in the form of Narasimha. This avatar is known to have appeared on earth to protect His devotee, Prahlada, from the evil king Hiranyakasipu. The name Narsi signifies the strength and courage of the Lord in protecting His devotees from harm and offers a reminder of His unwavering love and protection.
